panels.figure_caption: Intracapsular vascular invasion identified by US and CEUS. Images from a 59‐year‐old female patient with pathologically confirmed EA‐FTC. (a, b) Conventional US shows a tumor embolus (blue arrows) in the margin of the tumor (white arrows). (c) After the patient's consent was obtained, perfluorobutane microbubbles (Sonazoid, GE HealthCare; 0.01 mL/kg) were administered intravenously. CEUS demonstrates no enhancement within the vessel (blue arrow). (d) Histological image confirms intracapsular vascular invasion (blue arrow) within the capsule (white double‐headed arrow) (hematoxylin and eosin, 4× magnification). CEUS, contrast‐enhanced ultrasonography; EA‐FTC, encapsulated angioinvasive follicular thyroid carcinoma; US, ultrasound.
in_text_mentions: The status of intracapsular vessels was evaluated. Dilated angioid structures within the capsule were deemed indicative of potential intracapsular angioinvasion. Contrast‐enhanced ultrasonography (CEUS) was conducted to confirm the presence of a tumor thrombus in intracapsular vessels. The characteristics of the intracapsular angioinvasion are illustrated in Figure 4.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Ultrasound image of a thyroid nodule with a thin hyperechoic rim (halo sign), a finding included in the follicular thyroid carcinoma vocabulary. The caption labels the lesion as FTN, but the article is focused on follicular thyroid carcinoma. b: Second ultrasound image in the same figure showing a thyroid nodule with a thin hyperechoic peripheral rim, consistent with the captioned sonographic halo sign. c: Gross pathology specimen of a well-circumscribed thyroid nodule with a fibrous capsule, matching the captioned gross FTN specimen and the follicular thyroid carcinoma vocabulary for a firm encapsulated nodule. d: H&E histopathology showing an encapsulated follicular neoplasm with an intact fibrous capsule, consistent with the captioned FTN capsule and the follicular thyroid carcinoma vocabulary.
panels.attribution_text: Yao et al. Prospective Validation of an Ultrasound Capsule-Based Model for Predicting Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma Without High-Risk Features.. Cancer medicine 2025. doi:10.1002/cam4.71190. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Sonographic and pathological features of the intact FTN capsule (grade 0). (a, b) Ultrasound images demonstrate a thin hyperechoic rim surrounding the nodule (arrows). (c) Gross specimen and (d) histopathological section confirm that the hyperechoic line on ultrasound corresponds to the fibrous capsule (arrows) of the FTN (hematoxylin and eosin, 2× magnification). FTN, follicular thyroid neoplasm. FTN, follicular thyroid neoplasm.
in_text_mentions: etween the FTN capsule and specimen margin was calculated. Finally, by delineating a line equivalent to the aforementioned distance from the thyroid gland margin on the US image, it was observed that the intact capsule corresponded to the hyperechoic line of the margin or the inner layer of the halo (Grade 0, Figure 2). Conversely, the invaded capsules were seen as disruptions in the hyperechoic line (Grade 1, Figure 3a), local tumor protrusions resembling mushroom‐like shapes or satellite nodules (Grade 2, Figure 3b), or extracapsular invasion marked by a fibrous capsule (Grade 3, Figure 3c).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: H&E thyroidectomy specimen from a patient with follicular thyroid carcinoma, showing vascular invasion in capsular vessels. B: Higher-power H&E of the same thyroidectomy specimen, demonstrating tumor within capsular vessels, supporting vascular invasion in follicular thyroid carcinoma. C: H&E of bone biopsy showing metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma with follicular-patterned neoplastic infiltration. D: High-power H&E of metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma in bone, confirming follicular-type neoplastic cells. E: Immunohistochemistry of bone metastasis showing TTF-1 positivity in follicular cells, supporting follicular thyroid carcinoma origin. F: Immunohistochemistry of bone metastasis showing thyroglobulin positivity in follicular cells, consistent with metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma.

panels.figure_caption: (A, B) Tumor cells in the liver formed follicular structures, some containing colloid (Hematoxylin and eosin, × 40). (C) Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for thyroglobulin ( × 40), which, in conjunction with the findings on hematoxylin and eosin staining, was consistent with metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma. in_text_mentions: were made: (1) To perform a robot-assisted laparoscopic left lateral hepatectomy to clarify the nature of the liver mass. (2) To place the lung nodules under active surveillance for the time being. Postoperative pathological examination of the liver mass indicated metastatic thyroid carcinoma (Figure 2). Immunohistochemistry revealed positivity for TTF-1, Tg, CK7, CK19, and CD56, and negativity for Galectin-3, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 5% in hotspot areas. In the setting of distant metastasis, these findings support a diagnosis of metastatic FTC, as confirmed on review.

igated. In our case, the fact that both mutations were present in the distant metastasis corroborates the idea that they both contributed to the aggressiveness of the tumor. panels.figure_caption: Macroscopic and histological attributes of the macrofollicular variant of follicular thyroid carcinoma (MV-FTC). a Cross-section of the gross specimen revealing a well-circumscribed, light brown lesion with a homogenous appearance. Note the macroscopically visible areas with capsular engagement. b Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stain at low power (✕ 40) magnification visualizing the circumscribed tumor with colloid-like, macrofollicular appearance. c H&E stain displaying the macrofollicular growth pattern at ✕ 100 magnification. There was a general lack of degenerative changes, which are usually seen in colloid nodules. Macrofollicles were defined as > 200 µm, which equals the size of the micron bar in the lower right corner. d H&E stain at high power (✕ 400) magnification displaying cellular details of the MV-FTC. Note the monotonous-looking nuclei lacking atypia lining the macro-follicles, with occasional, more hypercellular areas. e H&E stain at ✕ 100 magnification highlighting the broad, fibrous tumor capsule. Normal thyroid tissue is seen to the right of the image. f Clear-cut capsular invasion with a broad, mushroom-like protrusion into the surrounding thyroid parenchyma (arrowhead). Several areas with capsular invasion were noted, but vascular invasion was absent

source_variant.figure_caption: Macroscopic and histological attributes of the macrofollicular variant of follicular thyroid carcinoma (MV-FTC). a Cross-section of the gross specimen revealing a well-circumscribed, light brown lesion with a homogenous appearance. Note the macroscopically visible areas with capsular engagement. b Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stain at low power (✕ 40) magnification visualizing the circumscribed tumor with colloid-like, macrofollicular appearance. c H&E stain displaying the macrofollicular growth pattern at ✕ 100 magnification. There was a general lack of degenerative changes, which are usually seen in colloid nodules. Macrofollicles were defined as > 200 µm, which equals the size of the micron bar in the lower right corner. d H&E stain at high power (✕ 400) magnification displaying cellular details of the MV-FTC. Note the monotonous-looking nuclei lacking atypia lining the macro-follicles, with occasional, more hypercellular areas. e H&E stain at ✕ 100 magnification highlighting the broad, fibrous tumor capsule. Normal thyroid tissue is seen to the right of the image. f Clear-cut capsular invasion with a broad, mushroom-like protrusion into the surrounding thyroid parenchyma (arrowhead). Several areas with capsular invasion were noted, but vascular invasion was absent

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 12 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L). A: Gross image of a large, diffuse, hemorrhagic FTC; article title and caption confirm FTC. B: H&E section of FTC; caption identifies FTC and image shows trabecular/solid growth. C: H&E section with arrowed vascular invasion, a diagnostic feature of FTC. D: IHC for TTF-1 in FTC; caption states deeply stained positive. E: IHC for thyroglobulin in FTC; caption states partially stained. F: IHC for CK7 in FTC; caption states deeply stained positive. G: IHC for CK pan in FTC; caption states partially stained. H: IHC for Ki67 in FTC; caption states proliferation index less than 1%. I: IHC for calcitonin in FTC; caption states negative, supporting FTC over medullary carcinoma. J: IHC for PTH in FTC; caption states negative. K: H&E of metastatic FTC in neck lymph node; caption and in-text confirm metastasis. L: Higher-power H&E of metastatic FTC in neck lymph node; caption and in-text confirm metastasis.

panels.figure_caption: Gross and histopathological sections of follicular thyroid carcinoma and metastatic lymph node. (A) Gross image of follicular thyroid carcinoma. (D–J) Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining of follicular thyroid carcinoma (magnification × 200) for (D) TTF-1, (E) TG, (F) CK 7, (G) CK pan, (H) Ki 67, (I) calcitonin, (J) PTH. TTF-1 and CK7 were deeply stained (positive), TG and CK pan were partially stained (partial positive), Ki67 proliferation index was less than 1%, calcitonin and PTH didn't stain (negative). (K,L) H&E staining of neck metastatic lymph node: (K) magnification × 16, (L) magnification × 400. Yellow dashed circle indicated the amplification part in the picture K, black arrow indicated the normal part of the metastatic lymph node.

panels.rationale: Single real-patient thyroid ultrasound from a case report of bilateral follicular thyroid carcinoma. The caption describes multiple thyroid nodules, the largest being a complex heterogeneous hyperechoic and cystic nodule with internal calcifications and increased perinodular vascularity. Although the ultrasound appearance is not pathognomonic, the disease-focused article and patient context support attribution to follicular thyroid carcinoma, and calcifications are a recognized ultrasound finding.

panels.rationale: Single CT panel from a case report titled as synchronous papillary and follicular thyroid carcinoma presenting as a large toxic nodule. The caption specifically documents a left thyroid mass causing right tracheal deviation, a manifestation included in the follicular thyroid carcinoma vocabulary. The disease-focused article title supports attribution to follicular thyroid carcinoma, though the caption itself does not specify the histologic subtype.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: H&E-stained histology from the index follicular thyroid carcinoma case showing extensive vascular invasion, a diagnostic feature of angioinvasive FTC. [raw subtype: angioinvasive] b: CD31/pan-cytokeratin double immunohistochemistry showing intravascular tumor deposits in the index FTC case, confirming vascular invasion. [raw subtype: angioinvasive] c: CD61 immunohistochemistry from the index FTC case demonstrating an in vivo thrombus; the thrombus is not a specific vocabulary finding for FTC, so it is proposed only.
panels.attribution_text: Condello et al. Spatial Transcriptomics in a Case of Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma Reveals Clone-Specific Dysregulation of Genes Regulating Extracellular Matrix in the Invading Front.. Endocrine pathology 2024. doi:10.1007/s12022-024-09798-0. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Histological attributes of the index case. a Hematoxylin-eosin-stained section depicting extensive vascular invasion. b Double stain (CD31 in brown, pan-cytokeratin in red) visualizing intravascular tumor deposits. c CD61 immunohistochemistry confirms an in vivo phenomenon with thrombus
in_text_mentions: The index case was a 45-mm encapsulated angioinvasive FTC derived from a 54-year-old female patient (Fig. 1a). The diagnosis was made using the 2022 WHO classification criteria, and differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma could be excluded as the mitotic index was 1/2 mm2, and no tumor necrosis was evident despite extensive sampling. Venous invasion was observed multifocally, and capsular invasion was also noted. There was no extrathyroidal extension, and surgical margins were negative. panels.figure_caption: Surveillance imaging after transoral robotic surgery led to the second diagnosis of recurrent follicular neoplasm. (A) Coronal CT image of the neck almost 3 months after resection of the retropharyngeal node, approximately 15 months after initial thyroidectomy and lymph node dissection, reveals a new mass (open circle) at the base of the neck in the prior location of the right lobe of the thyroid. (B) Subsequently performed axial FDG PET/CT image shows mild FDG uptake within this mass (open circle), concerning for recurrent disease. (C) Transverse ultrasound image of the thyroid bed redemonstrates this mass (white arrow). An ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration performed on the same day was positive for follicular neoplasm. FDG: fluorodeoxyglucose
in_text_mentions: Approximately 19 months after presentation, surveillance CT revealed a new 2.3 cm nodule in the low right thyroidectomy bed (Figure 3). FDG PET/CT and ultrasound-guided FNA (Figure 3) one month later confirmed an FDG-avid follicular neoplasm consistent with the patient's known follicular carcinoma, representing the patient’s second locoregional recurrence. Three months after this latest recurrence, the patient underwent revision level 6 and 7 dissection, and the patient has had no evidence of disease at approximately two months following this procedure.

in_text_mentions: computed tomography (CT) scan showed a 14 × 8 cm tumor in the left 3rd to 6th ribs and multiple small lung nodules (Figure 1). Core-needle biopsy was performed on the left chest wall tumor. Hematoxylin-eosin staining (Figure 2A) revealed follicular growth in the tumor specimen obtained and immunohistochemical staining was positive for Tg (Figure 2B) and thyroid transcription factor-1 (Figure 2C). in_text_mentions: Medical treatment with NSAIDs and paracetamol was initiated, along with partial weight bearing and relative rest with no improvement at follow-up at 4 weeks. Surgical intervention was decided due to the persistent pain. The cyst was resected with a margin of surrounding fibro-osseous tissue and the bone grafted. Histopathological evaluation revealed a metastatic carcinoma of the thyroid gland. Immunostaining showed that the cells expressed cytokeratin, cytokeratin 7, and thyroglobulin, all of which confirm the diagnosis (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Single sagittal PET-CT fusion image from a case report of follicular thyroid carcinoma presenting with a large sternal metastasis. The caption and in-text description attribute the intensely hypermetabolic expansile lytic sternal lesion and the enlarged multinodular thyroid gland compressing the trachea to this patient's follicular thyroid carcinoma, so the panel is a real patient image showing a clinical manifestation (metastatic bone lesion, tracheal deviation from thyroid mass) of the configured disease. Sternal bone metastasis is a recognized but uncommon presentation (variant). The sternal lytic lesion and hypermetabolic thyroid/lung lesions are not covered by the provided vocabulary and are listed as proposed findings.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Gross lung resection specimen from a patient with follicular thyroid carcinoma showing a metastatic tumor with intra-tumoral cavitation and a necrotic/hemorrhagic cut surface; the cavitating anaplastic-transformed pulmonary metastasis is an unusual (atypical) presentation of the FTC-derived tumor. B: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of the FTC-derived pulmonary metastasis showing highly pleomorphic, hyperchromatic tumor cells consistent with anaplastic transformation of follicular thyroid carcinoma; the dedifferentiated pleomorphic pattern is atypical for follicular thyroid carcinoma. C: Immunohistochemical staining for PAX8 is strongly positive in the tumor cells, supporting a thyroid follicular cell origin of the metastatic tumor in this case of follicular thyroid carcinoma with anaplastic transformation. D: Immunohistochemical staining for TTF-1 is negative in the tumor cells; the loss of TTF-1 expression accompanies the anaplastic...

in_text_mentions: Histopathological evaluation of the resected lung (Figure 4A) revealed that the enlarged tumor was highly pleomorphic (Figure 4B), paired-box gene 8 (PAX8) positive (Figure 4C), and thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1) negative (Figure 4D), compatible with anaplastic thyroid carcinoma [7].

panels.rationale: Single real-patient FNAC photomicrograph of a scalp swelling in a case of metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma; caption and article explicitly attribute the follicular cell population with microfollicles and low-grade nuclear features to follicular thyroid carcinoma. The unusual scalp metastatic site makes the presentation atypical.
